extracted.intended_audience: editors, copyholders, proofreaders, typesetters, and authors preparing manuscripts for publication (University of Chicago Press / book and periodical publishing)
extracted.subtask_description: A publishing style manual for copyediting, punctuation, capitalization, hyphenation, typography, and typesetting rules used by editors, proofreaders, and compositors. Covers detailed rules for punctuation, italics, headings, tables, word division, spacing, and indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comma: general rules and many special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and illustrations of use of comma; many specific rules about where commas are used or omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes omission between two adjectives; in signatures and after author's name at beginning of articles; use after digits indicating thousands; before 'and,' 'or,' and 'nor'; before 'of' in connection with residence or position; omission between consecutive pages; use between month and year; with adjectival phrases; omitted before 'rather'; with adverbial clauses; with antithetical clauses; with appositional clauses; with brief quotations or maxims; with clauses ending in different prepositions; with conjunctions, adverbs, connective particles, and phrases; with parenthetical clauses; with participial clauses; to indicate omissions; to separate identical or similar words; to separate numbers; to separate proper nouns; rules for use summarized (see X41-62).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashes: definition, sizes, and rules for use
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and illustrations of use of dashes; different sizes explained and illustrated; rules for use of dashes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use at end of word/phrase implied at beginning of each succeeding paragraph; for emphasis; with literary references; with parenthetical clauses; with complementary clauses; to connect numbers; to denote break, stop, transition, or change in sentence; to precede summarizing clauses; to indicate implication of word or phrase; to indicate pause, transition, or epigrammatic turn; use of em, en, two-em, three-em dashes described (see 166-75, 261).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphens & Hyphenization: rules and lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of hyphens and hyphenization; list of hyphenated words and hyphen leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of consecutive hyphens allowable at ends of lines; hyphen used to indicate omission of element common to two or more compounds; hyphen use with many prefixes/suffixes (by-, co-, pre-, re-, extra-, infra-, pan-, supra-, ultra-, ante-, anti-, inter-, intra-, post-, sub-, super-, fold, great, like, un-, in-, a-, non-, over-, under-, quasi-, semi-, demi-, tri-, bi-, vice-, ex-, elect-, general-, lieutenant); hyphenation rules 183-314; hyphenated words division to be avoided; list of hyphenated words (314).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound words and compounds: formation and capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on compounds: when to hyphenate; capitalization of nouns forming parts of compounds; special classes of compounds (father, mother, brother, sister, daughter, parent, foster, fellow, god, half, quarter, life, world, maker, dealer, master, self, skin, store, shop, room, house, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific rules for compounds with by-, co-, pre-, re-, extra-, infra-, pan-, supra-, ultra-, ante-, anti-, inter-, intra-, post-, sub-, super-, fold, great, like, un-, in-, a-, non-, over-, under-, quasi-, semi-, tri-, bi-, vice-, ex-, elect-, general-, lieutenant; omission of common element indicated by hyphen; omission of component elements in compound words to be indicated (see entries 183-314 and examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization: general principles and principal words in titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization of principal words in titles of publications, documents, essays, pamphlets, papers, plays, poems, periodicals, series, tracts, treatises, transactions, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of capitals in English, Latin, French, Italian, Spanish, Scandinavian, German, Danish, Dutch titles; when titles are italicized or roman-quoted; definition of principal words (see 41, 60, 80-83, 92-105).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization: names of organizations, institutions, and industrial/commercial bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization rules for names of commercial firms, organizations, institutions, industrial organizations, social and educational organizations and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treatment of 'Company' when abbreviated in firm names; capitalization specifics for University of Chicago divisions and departments (see entries xx, 49, 207).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization: political and governmental names
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization of names of Congress, legislative bodies, judiciary bodies, departments, governmental offices, sessions, and members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names of houses of Congress capitalized; sessions of Congress capitalized; members to be lower-cased; numbers of sessions spelled out; capitalization of names of legislative bodies, regiments, armies, parties, alliances, political divisions (see 12-13, 21, 100, 6-7, 9, 11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization: religious and sacred names
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization rules for denominations, creeds, confessions of faith, creeds, sacred books, New and Old Testament books, parables, Trinity, Trinity members, names for Supreme Being and pronouns referring to Deity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists and abbreviations for Old and New Testament books; capitalization of names of religious organizations, sects, monastic orders, and honorifics; rules for 'Saint' and abbreviations ('St.') (see 9, 19, 24, 108-109).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization: geographical names, divisions, regions, and thoroughfares
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization of place-names, regions or parts of the world, squares, parks, towns and states, divisions of countries, and thoroughfares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for numbered political divisions spelled out; when 'State' is capitalized; lists and rules for states and territories abbreviations and when to abbreviate (see 4-8, 28, 106).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization: personal names, titles, honorifics, and nobility
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of given names, Christian names, family-name particles (Mac/Mc/M'), clerical titles, military/civil titles, honorary titles, nobility, and indexing rules for particles (Van, Ten, 'Mac','Mc', 'M').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules when titles are capitalized or lower-cased, handling of titles preceding names, when to abbreviate academic degrees and titles, and indexing of particles (see 21, 22, 31, 340, 49).

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics and italicizing: definition and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of italics and rules for use of italics and what to set in roman versus italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Italicize titles of books and other works, titles of legal causes and proceedings, names of genera and species, letters designating unknown quantities, words and phrases from foreign languages, emphasis, initial words 'Resolved' in resolutions, catalogue names, names of newspapers (including city when necessary); rules and exceptions (see 58-73, 60-71, 82-83).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation marks and quotations: rules for use and punctuation placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of double and single quotation marks; when to omit quotation marks (e.g., with preface, index); punctuation placement (period, comma, colon, semicolon, exclamation, interrogation point) in relation to quotation marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotation marks not used with reduced citations except in exceptions; placement of comma, period, colon, semicolon, exclamation point, and interrogation point relative to quotation marks detailed (see 74-98, 126-140).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipses: rules for use and treatment as part of quotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of ellipses; ellipses treated as part of quotation; use to indicate omissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See rules 280-282; use of ellipses for omissions; exceptions and formatting guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parentheses and parenthetical clauses: usage and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of parentheses, placement of periods in connection with parentheses, and use of brackets for interpolations or material within parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parentheses used for parenthetical clauses, subdivisions, and within parentheses use brackets; placement rules for period/other punctuation; interaction with indices and enumerations (see 176-178, 136, 150-177).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parenthetical and participial clauses: comma and dash usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on punctuation (commas, dashes, parentheses) with parenthetical, participial, and other subordinate clauses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of commas with participial clauses; commas and dashes for parenthetical clauses; dashes for emphasis or summarizing clauses; parentheses for interpolations (see 148-169, 177).

rubrics_metrics.name: Semicolon: uses and enumerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of semicolon to separate distinct clauses in enumerations and to mark division of sentence; placement with quotation marks and scripture references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in enumerations; comparison illustration with comma; semicolon to separate passages in Scripture references containing chapters; rules 237-240 and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colon: use with 'namely' and in explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of colon in various constructions including before explanations and after words like 'namely.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Namely,' use of colon in connection with, 130; general guidance for explanatory material and lists (see 13a, 351-354 for technical explanations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Period (full stop): placement and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for placing the period relative to quotation marks and exceptions (omission after headlines, Roman numerals, certain abbreviations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit period after headlines and running heads; omit after Roman numerals and some initials; use of period after abbreviations for linguistic epochs; rules 133-136, and classical reference exceptions (337, 339).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers and numerals: spelling and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of numbers beginning a sentence, consecutive numbers, numbers in groups, round numbers, use of comma to separate thousands, treatment of numbers less than three digits (spelled out), use of dash for 'to' connecting numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consecutive numbers treated alike; groups of six or more closely connected set in figures; use comma after digits indicating thousands; numbers of less than three digits to be spelled out in ordinary reading-matter; rules 94-96, 154-159, 173.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates and decades: punctuation and spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for dates: when to spell out decades, omission of st, d, th in dates, comma between month and year, treatment of publication dates following volume numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decades to be spelled out; omission of j, d, and th in dates; comma use between month and year; dates of publications follow volume numbers; see entries 100-102, 159-160, 237.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations and initials: spacing, periods, and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of abbreviations like E.g., I.e., F., ff., MS, P.M., initialisms and initials in titles of publications; omission of periods in some contexts; spacing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g. and I.e. to be set in roman; period to be omitted after initials used as abbreviations for publications; spacing for P.M.; separation of initials in different lines to be avoided; see 53, 62, 133, 319, 339.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes and indices: numbering, placement, and style
rubrics_metrics.description: General style and exceptions for footnotes, numbering, placement of index figure, indices for references to footnotes, and use of symbols (dagger, double dagger, paragraph mark, parallel mark).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbering rules (339), placing of index figure (336), sequences and what to use for reference indices, rules for footnotes to tables, samples and exceptions noted (see 332-339, 23a, 35a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing rules: italics in cross-references and treatment of particles
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for indexing: italicizing 'See' and 'See also' in cross-references, treatment of prefixes and particles in proper nouns, indexing of names with particles, and sequence rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Italicize 'See' and 'See also' in cross-references; rules for particles like 'Van', 'Ten', 'Mac', 'Mc'; sequence and cross-reference conventions (see 63, 340).

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of words and word division: systems and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and systems for dividing words at line ends, etymological divisions to avoid, avoidance of dividing on two letters or at certain letters, treatment of diphthongs and digraphs, and division of foreign words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules 215-231; system of division 22x; avoid division on two letters, avoid division of short words, avoid certain divisions (soft g, j, etc.); use hyphen to indicate syllable division; etymological division to be avoided; see 225-231, 331-337 for foreign languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing and spaces: sizes and standard spacing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of different sizes of spaces (thin, thick, em, en, hair, three-em, etc.), rules for spacing in foundry, linotype, and monotype composition, and standard spacing guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens and samples of lines spaced with different sizes; spacing effect on etymological divisions; spacing of divisional signs, figure columns in tables, formulae, headlines, metric symbols, monetary symbols, numerals at beginning of paragraphs, reading-matter in tables, rules 358-373 and samples (see 261, 359-364, 368-373).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and tabular work: open vs ruled, headlines, and setting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for setting tables, headlines for open and ruled tables, specimen tables, spacing and rules for rules and leaders in tables, and typographic treatment of columns (percentages, totals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-column tables set as open; tables of more than two as ruled; box-heads for ruled tables; columns representing totals or percentages sometimes set off by distinctive type; rules 241-250, specimen tables 250, 341-350; reading-matter in ruled tables and spacing guidelines (342-346).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings, headlines, running heads, cut-in-heads, side-heads: setting and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and guidance for headings, headlines, running heads, cut-in-heads, side-heads and their punctuation and capitalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission of period after headlines, running heads, side-heads, and legends; spacing of headlines; 'Continued' and 'To be continued' set in italics or brackets and reduced type at end of articles; use of lower case for side-heads in some cases; use of dashes with side-heads (see 73, 125, 135, 172, 179, 280-384).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs, galleys, page-proofs and make-up: definitions and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and descriptions of galley, galley-proof, page-proof, plate-proof, make-up, foul proof, and instructions for proofreaders and copyholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints to proofreaders and editors (pp. 113-116, 127-129), definitions and descriptions (285-289, 385-389), revision and revise defined; rules for numbering footnotes in linotype/monotype composition; proof samples and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography: type sizes, styles, and technical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and names for sizes of type, styles of type, faces (roman, italic, small caps), technical typographical terms (quads, em, en, pica, pearl, shank, shoulder, kern, slug, leaded, solid, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation of different parts of body of type, names for sizes and styles, definitions of terms (351-94, 252-357) and how to indicate styles in copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation of extracts and literary references
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for punctuation of extracts from modern authors, literary references, abbreviations used in references, and reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When to reduce extracts, when to run quotations into text, punctuation rules for literary references and classical references; lists of abbreviations used in literary references and punctuation specifics (85-91, 337-339).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of italics and quotation for foreign words and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of foreign words and phrases: italicize foreign words or phrases, include English equivalent quoted or roman-quoted, and translation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English equivalent to be quoted; system of division for foreign words; sentences and passages quoted from foreign languages treated specially; translation of names of foreign institutions and foreign words (59-60, 78, 331).

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent and percentages: numeric expression and tabular presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Per cent to be expressed in figures and not treated as an abbreviation; percentages in tables sometimes set in distinctive type; columns of percentages formatting guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percent expressed in figures (94); not treated as abbreviation (133); table presentation notes (342).

rubrics_metrics.name: Superscripts and superior figures: use for reference indices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of superior figures (superscripts) for reference indices and rules for placing indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for footnote indices and references; placing of index figure and sequence rules (232, 333-336).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation and interrogation marks for questions and exclamations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for using interrogation and exclamation points: direct questions followed by interrogation point; indirect questions not; use of exclamation point for outcry and irony; use of exclamatory 'Oh'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct questions followed by interrogation point; indirect not; exclamation point uses 127, 137-139; differentiation between 'O' and 'Oh' (117).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indices, reference indices, and sequences: ordering and symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: What to use for reference indices, sequences of footnote indices, and use of symbols (dagger, double dagger, paragraph mark, parallel mark).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indices for footnote references: how to number and place (333-336); use of dagger and double dagger for footnote index (35a, 93a); paragraph mark spacing and use (369, 23a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of brackets for interpolations, explanations, and omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of brackets for interpolations and explanatory insertions and to indicate omission; guidelines for bracket use within parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpolations set with brackets (178); use brackets inside parentheses; brackets used to indicate omissions or explanatory material in quoted or printed text (178, 280).
